text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR first. It spots routing flaws without touching live code, so we learn before we act. The trade-off is delayed feedback on other PRs, but we avoid breaking changes. This keeps self-improvement safe and data-driven.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on the newest open PR risks exposing *new* edge cases that could mislead us—those flaws might not exist in the oldest merged PR, so we’d validate a path that’s already broken. Better to run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the *oldest merged PR* first; it tests the most stable routing path, so any issues we find are real regressions, not noise. Settle it by measuring how many routing flaws PR-Agent flags in each scenario and comparing their severity.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *both* the oldest merged PR and the newest open PR simultaneously—this doubles the data points for routing flaws without adding extra runs, cutting time in half while keeping the safety of testing stable and unstable paths. The trade-off is slightly higher compute cost, but it’s cheaper than running separate tests and faster than waiting for sequential results.
